evidence.title: Tunisia softens its ‘false news’ penalty. What really changed, and why now?

occurrences.checkable_against: Official text of the amendment to Tunisia Decree 54
occurrences.quote_span: The amendment to Decree 54, which went into effect on Wednesday, sets fines of 10,000 to 20,000 Tunisian dinars ($3,370 to $6,740) for a first offence of spreading “false news” and related violations.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Lotfi Hajji's statement and SNJT/civil society demands
occurrences.quote_span: Lotfi Hajji, head of Al Jazeera’s bureau in Tunisia, said civil society groups and the journalists’ union were demanding Decree 54 be scrapped altogether, so that journalists could be judged under the 2011 press freedom law instead.
occurrences.speaker: Lotfi Hajji
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: SNJT documentation and declaration concerning Decree 54 trials
occurrences.quote_span: The National Syndicate of Tunisian Journalists (SNJT) documented that hundreds of journalists, bloggers, opposition politicians, lawyers and activists had been tried under the decree since it came into force in 2022, and declared the situation an “emergency”.
occurrences.speaker: National Syndicate of Tunisian Journalists
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Kais Saied's public statements on his rule and Decree 54
occurrences.quote_span: Saied rejects accusations of autocratic rule, saying his actions are legal and are needed to end years of disorder and alleged corruption.
occurrences.speaker: Kais Saied
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Said Benarbia's statement to Al Jazeera
occurrences.quote_span: The reduction in penalties was a “positive development”, Benarbia of the International Commission of Jurists said, but what was required was an end to all abusive prosecutions and the release of those arbitrarily detained under the decree.
occurrences.speaker: Said Benarbia
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Rafik Abdessalem's statement to Al Jazeera
occurrences.quote_span: Rafik Abdessalem, Tunisia’s foreign minister from 2011 to 2013 and a senior figure in the Islamist Ennahdha party, said the decree had been used “to silence every voice critical of the regime”.
occurrences.speaker: Rafik Abdessalem
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Official text of Tunisia Decree 54 and its amendment
occurrences.quote_span: Anyone who reoffended faced six months behind bars on top of a 50,000-dinar fine (more than $16,000).
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Official text of the amendment to Tunisia Decree 54
occurrences.quote_span: The fines replace a five-year prison sentence. However, repeat offenders may still face jail.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Official text of Tunisia Decree 54 and its amendment
occurrences.quote_span: Targeting a public official or a person of equivalent status raised the ceiling to a decade behind bars and a fine of 100,000 dinars (more than $32,000).
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Rafik Abdessalem's statement to Al Jazeera
occurrences.quote_span: “In short, the punishment has been reduced, but its repressive and punitive character remains unchanged,” Abdessalem told Al Jazeera.
occurrences.speaker: Rafik Abdessalem
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: European Parliament statements and resolutions on Tunisia Decree 54
occurrences.quote_span: Among international critics of the decree are Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch and the European Parliament, which has described it as “a tool to interfere with fundamental freedoms” and called for its repeal.
occurrences.speaker: European Parliament
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Tunisian parliamentary records on proposed Decree 54 and press-law reforms
occurrences.quote_span: Proposals in parliament since 2024 for a wider overhaul have been ignored.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Rafik Abdessalem's statement to Al Jazeera
occurrences.quote_span: The amendment aimed to make the image of Saied’s Tunisia “less bleak” after it has become associated with “trials, arrests and the use of arbitrary decrees,” he said.
occurrences.speaker: Rafik Abdessalem
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Official Tunisian government statements on Decree 54
occurrences.quote_span: The government, meanwhile, says the decree protects people and public order from attack, and is needed to tackle online crime and disinformation.
occurrences.speaker: Tunisian government
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Announcement and plans for the nationwide march by Tunisian civil society groups and the labour union
occurrences.quote_span: Hours before Wednesday’s amendment came into effect, civil society groups spearheaded by Tunisia’s largest labour union unveiled plans for a nationwide march over what they regarded as restrictions on civil liberties.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Said Benarbia's statement to Al Jazeera
occurrences.quote_span: The law was “one of the potent tools of oppression used by the government to crush dissent, crack down on civic space and arbitrarily restrict the freedom of expression in the country,” Said Benarbia, Middle East and North Africa director of the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ), told Al Jazeera.
occurrences.speaker: Said Benarbia
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54

occurrences.checkable_against: Official text of Tunisia Decree 54 and its amendment
occurrences.quote_span: The penalties doubled when the offence was aimed at a public official or someone of equivalent status.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Tunisia Decree 54
